item.title: 70 Americans still unaccounted for after catastrophic Nepal flooding
item.description: Officials say 70 Americans remain unaccounted for after catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border, while warning the region remains too dangerous for travelers.
item.content:encoded:
The State Department said Tuesday it is aware of approximately 70 Americans who remain unaccounted for in the Nepal-China border region following last month's catastrophic flooding, while 18 Americans have now made it to safety.

"We extend our deepest sympathy to all those affected by the flooding in Nepal, and their families, and we reaffirm our enduring friendship with the Nepali people," a State Department official told Fox News.

"The Department of State remains in close contact with the families of Americans who remain unaccounted for and is committed to providing regular updates as more information becomes available."

ROUGHLY 80 AMERICANS STILL UNACCOUNTED FOR AFTER HIMALAYAN DISASTER KILLS 903, OFFICIALS SAY

Officials also urged Americans not to travel to the disaster zone, warning the region remains at risk for additional flash floods and landslides.

The latest update reduced the number of Americans unaccounted for from 75 to 70, while the number confirmed safe rose from 16 to 18.

Officials have not confirmed any American deaths.

RESCUERS USE ZIPLINES TO TRANSPORT TRAPPED CITIZENS AFTER DEVASTATING NEPAL FLOODS DECIMATE COUNTRY'S BRIDGES

As search efforts continue, Nepalese authorities said rescuers are concentrating on three hydropower project tunnels where they believe dozens of workers may still be trapped beneath debris left by the Aug. 26 glacier collapse that triggered devastating flooding along the Nepal-China border, according to Reuters.

"Our search operation is focused on finding survivors, including in tunnels. Our bigger focus is on the Chilime hydroelectric project, where we believe people are trapped, because there was a canteen, residency and arrangements for food," Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of Nepal's disaster authority, told Reuters.

DEATH TOLL FROM MUDSLIDES, FLOODING AT NEPAL-CHINA BORDER CLIMBS PAST 670; NEARLY 3,000 MISSING

The disaster has killed at least 1,399 people across Nepal and China's Tibet region, with more than 5,400 others still missing, according to authorities. 

Both governments have blamed climate change for the glacier collapse that unleashed the flooding.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: 'The View' co-host demands 25th Amendment be used against Trump, suggests Cabinet could do it after midterms
item.description: Sunny Hostin raised invoking the 25th Amendment against President Donald Trump on "The View," speculating the Cabinet could act if Republicans lose the House and Senate.
item.content:encoded:
"The View" co-host Sunny Hostin raised using the 25th Amendment against President Donald Trump on Tuesday, as the ABC talk show returned from its summer break.

"My question is when do we really start, in earnest — and I mean this honestly — considering the 25th Amendment," Hostin said.

"I think when the Republicans lose the House, and they lose the Senate, they’re going to want to have some control over this person, this person that is in the office, and JD Vance would then be that replacement and I wonder if the Cabinet then looks at each other and says, ‘OK, we’ve got to take control of this, 25th Amendment,’" she added.

The 25th Amendment to the Constitution empowers a president’s Cabinet to remove him from office if he is unable to do the job.

PUSH TO OUST TRUMP EXPOSES CRACKS AMONG DEMOCRATS ON STRATEGY, TIMING

Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin pushed back, saying she didn't think Trump's Cabinet would ever take such action. 

"I think if they didn’t do it after January 6, in that period before he left office [in 2021], it’s never going to happen," she said.

The White House did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Co-hosts Whoopi Goldberg and Joy Behar have also called for the use of the 25th Amendment against Trump since he returned to office last year.

JEN PSAKI SHUTS DOWN 25TH AMENDMENT TALK ABOUT TRUMP, DECLARES IT'S 'NOT GOING TO HAPPEN'

While criticizing Trump's efforts to resolve the war between Russia and Ukraine in September 2025, Goldberg said, "He had an opportunity to do so much more than he offered them, and they don’t consider him to be serious anymore, and I’m worried. What is the amendment, the 20-"

The co-hosts took their guesses at which amendment Goldberg was referencing, making multiple attempts before Hostin eventually informed them that it was the 25th Amendment.

"They questioned Biden’s competence," Goldberg said at the time. "If Biden had acted like this, I would have said take him and sit him down somewhere, but this was not — this was not presidential, and this was not helpful."

After Trump unveiled plaques beneath portraits of his predecessors, including Barack Obama and Joe Biden, on the new White House Presidential Walk of Fame in December 2025, Behar asked when the Cabinet would push to remove the president.

"When are they going to invoke the 25th Amendment? Does he have to run naked into the White House or what? What is that amendment for if not for this?" Behar said, drawing laughter from the audience.

FCC CHAIR MOCKS 'THE VIEW' HOST SUNNY HOSTIN FOR BLATANT PARTISANSHIP AS SHE PLEADS FOR DEMS TO WIN SENATE

"The View" launched a campaign seeking public support in June amid a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) investigation into the liberal talk show as the agency cracks down on equal time for political candidates after Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico joined the co-hosts for an interview.

ABC’s campaign features a petition to declare that "The View" qualifies as a bona fide news interview program. A commercial debuted in June during the program declared, "’The View has welcomed your favorite guests for nearly 30 years. Now the FCC wants to control who is allowed to appear on the show. Tell the FCC to let the viewers decide."

item.title: Trump's unusual role at midterm convention revealed as schedule goes public
item.description: Trump headlines both nights of the RNC's first-ever GOP midterm convention in Dallas, with JD Vance delivering the Thursday keynote speech.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE — DALLAS — With an eye toward energizing the GOP's MAGA base, the Republican National Committee (RNC) on Tuesday announced the speaking order and times of this week's first-ever GOP midterm convention, and President Donald Trump will be the Primetime headliner both nights.

According to the list, which was shared first with Fox News Digital on the eve of the convention, the president will deliver Wednesday's keynote address, which is tentatively scheduled to start at 9 p.m. ET.

Trump will return on Thursday evening at the American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas to close out the convention, with remarks after Vice President JD Vance gives the second night's keynote speech.

With less than two months to go until the midterm elections, Trump and Republicans are gathering in Texas for their historic confab as they aim to energize the party's base ahead of key races that will determine whether the GOP keeps control of Congress. Supporters of the president traditionally do not turn out in robust numbers when Trump is not on the ballot.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Democrats and Republicans traditionally hold large nominating conventions during presidential election years. But Trump last year floated the idea of a similar gathering ahead of the midterms to showcase the signature policy achievements he and Republicans in Congress have produced over the past two years.

The president called the convention "a truly Historic Event" and "a RALLY like none other!" when he announced it earlier this summer.

The convention comes as Republicans face energized Democrats and stiff political headwinds as they defend their slim House and Senate majorities in the midterms.

But Republicans are expected to paint a contrast, as they use the convention to spotlight the Democrats' leftward lurch and tie the entire Democratic Party to far-left and socialist proposals.

"The midterm election is about the future of our country. President Donald Trump and Republicans are fighting to launch the golden age of America while extreme liberal Democrats want to tear this country apart and create a liberal failed state with their out-of-touch and anti-American views,"," Republican National Committee chair Joe Gruters argued in a statement to Fox News Digital.

THESE 12 MIDTERM RACES WILL DECIDE WHICH PARTY CONTROLS THE SENATE

Gruters emphasized that "the choice is clear in November and the American people will reject these liberal policies and deliver historic wins for Republicans across the country."

The DNC, which remains in debt and decided against holding a similar convention, sees the GOP confab as a chance to blast Republicans.

"While everyday Americans struggle to pay their bills, fill up their tanks, or put food on the table, Republicans are hosting a multi-million dollar celebration to satisfy an aging and erratic Trump and tie vulnerable Republican candidates closer to his failed agenda,"," DNC Rapid Response Director Kendall Witmer charged.

Witmer argued that "Americans don’t want a ‘Trumpapalooza’ — they want lower costs and affordable healthcare."

The convention will also serve as the GOP's closing argument heading into November. In the fight for the Senate majority, Republican candidates in some of the most crucial races will also address the convention.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the GOP nominee in Texas who is facing off against Democratic state Rep. James Talarico in the race to replace Republican Sen. John Cornyn, will speak on the first evening. So will former RNC Chair Mike Whatley, who is defending retiring GOP Sen. Thom Tillis' seat in battleground North Carolina.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio, who is in a pitched fight with former longtime Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, will also address the crowd, as will Rep. Mike Collins of Georgia, the Republican challenger taking on Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in swing state Georgia.

Former Rep. Mike Rogers of Michigan, who is hoping to flip a Democrat-held open seat in the key Great Lakes battleground as he runs against far-left Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, speaks on Thursday evening.

In the battle for the House, where the GOP holds a razor-thin majority, incumbents and candidates in competitive races will also be in the speaking spotlight.

They include Reps. Monica De La Cruz of Texas, Derrick Van Orden of Wisconsin, Rob Bresnahan of Pennsylvania, and candidates Mike LiPetri of New York and Jay Feely of Arizona on Wednesday night.

Among the House Republican incumbents and candidates in close races speaking on Thursday are Reps. Ryan Mackenzie of Pennsylvania and Mike Lawler of New York, along with nominees Greg Cunningham of New Mexico, Derrick Merrin of Ohio and Eric Flores of Texas.

STATE OF PLAY: WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN IN THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS

Speaker Mike Johnson will speak on Thursday evening, according to the RNC schedule.

Johnson's Senate counterpart, Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-South Dakota), is notably absent from the list of speakers released by the RNC. But a source familiar with the planning tells Fox News Digital that Thune will be in Dallas, with a full schedule that includes helping Senate candidates fundraise.

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who is running for a fourth term leading the Lone Star State, speaks on Thursday. So does Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas, the conservative firebrand who is not on the ballot this year but could make a second White House bid in 2028.

Meanwhile, some of the biggest names in Trump's Cabinet are scheduled to speak, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Wednesday evening, and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who spearheaded the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement, on Thursday evening.

item.title: Virginia county to pay up to $2K to families with primary wage earner detained by ICE
item.description: Arlington County approved $50,000 to support immigrant families whose primary wage earner has been detained amid Trump administration enforcement efforts.
item.content:encoded:
Leaders in one Virginia county approved a program last week to set aside $50,000 to support families in which the primary wage earner has been detained by federal immigration authorities.

In a special Sept. 2 meeting, the Arlington County Board voted 4-0 to appropriate the funds, which will be distributed by Arlington Thrive, which describes itself as a "key component of the social safety net" in partnership with the county government.

Under the program, eligible families will receive up to $2,000 for those who have lost the primary wage earner. Arlington Thrive aims to assist between 25 to 30 families, according to the board's agenda.

HOW GUARANTEED INCOME ADVOCATES STRIVE TO TURN CASH ASSISTANCE INTO POLICY AFTER COVID-RELIEF FUNDS DRIED UP

"We stand with our immigrant families, and we will not stop doing so," Board Chair Matt de Ferranti said. "We are valuing the families of those that have been displaced and removed."

The move was in response to the Trump administration's illegal immigration enforcement efforts in the Washington, D.C., area in recent months.

"Ensuring that we take care of our community and our residents and our people does mean making sure that we have emergency assistance available for what is probably one of the most challenging situations that you could possibly face," Board Vice Chair Maureen Coffey said. "I'm very proud of us for doing this."

SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW

The funds will be distributed to families in the form of debit cards and checks.

Elizabeth Matlock, a staff member in the county manager’s office who is coordinating the effort, said the organization is ready to begin issuing funds.

"Thrive is eager to get started with this project," she said.

The vote came as officers with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) quietly made more than 1,300 arrests of illegal immigrants over 14 days in the Washington, D.C., suburbs last month.

Of those arrested, almost 400 illegal immigrants had criminal convictions or pending criminal charges, including a Salvadoran national wanted in Richmond, Virginia, on a murder warrant. Other crimes included rape, sexual assault, kidnapping, DUI, robbery and attempted murder.

item.title: US warns Americans about exit bans and 'unjust' detention in popular destination
item.description: The U.S. State Department is warning Americans traveling to China about exit bans, arbitrary detention and surveillance of private electronic messages.
item.content:encoded:
Americans who may be planning a trip to China are urged to take extra precautions, as U.S. officials warn travelers to "keep a low profile" while visiting the country.

The State Department recently updated its Level 2 "Exercise Increased Caution" advisory for mainland China, warning Americans about the arbitrary enforcement of local laws, exit bans and "the risk of unjust arrest or detention."

U.S. citizens could be questioned or detained without being told what crime they are accused of — and without being given access to U.S. consular services, according to the advisory.

AMERICANS HEADED FOR HIGH-RISK NATION URGED TO PREPARE WILLS, LEAVE DNA SAMPLES AHEAD OF TIME

"U.S. citizens in China may also face interrogations and detention without fair and transparent treatment under the law," the State Department warns.

The advisory notes that business people, academics and journalists are among those who have faced questioning, detention or expulsion for alleged violations of China's national security laws.

"U.S. citizens might only become aware of an exit ban when they attempt to depart China," the advisory states.

The State Department said the restrictions have been used to pressure people to participate in investigations, resolve civil disputes and compel relatives or associates to return to China.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

In some cases, exit bans have remained in place for years, preventing U.S. citizens from leaving the country even to receive medical treatment, according to the advisory.

Officials are also warning Americans to be careful about what they say and share electronically while traveling.

"Assume that China's security services can read your emails, texts, and social media posts if you send them to or from China," the advisory states.

The State Department warns that Americans could be detained or deported for private electronic messages critical of China, Hong Kong, Macau or the Chinese Communist Party. 

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Authorities have detained people over messages sent while they were outside China, according to the advisory.

For Americans who decide to travel to mainland China, officials recommend avoiding demonstrations and being cautious around large gatherings.

Travelers are also advised to avoid sharing opinions either publicly or privately that Chinese authorities could consider embarrassing or negative and to avoid photographing protesters or police without permission.

"Keep a low profile," the State Department advises.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The updated advisory also includes separate guidance for Hong Kong and Macau.

Americans are advised to exercise increased caution in Hong Kong due to the arbitrary enforcement of local laws. 

Macau carries a higher Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" advisory due to similar concerns and the U.S. government's limited ability to provide emergency consular services there.

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for comment and further information.

item.title: Government land-grab agenda hits key Senate race as Dem backs property takeovers echoing Mamdani
item.description: Maine Senate candidate Troy Jackson suggested the state should take over mobile home parks, echoing NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani's housing agenda.
item.content:encoded:
Graham Platner’s replacement in the Maine Senate race suggested the government should be able to take over private property when necessary, appearing to echo socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s housing agenda.

Troy Jackson, a Democrat running for the Senate, came under fire for suggesting the government should be able to take over private property when necessary. The comments drew fresh scrutiny to a candidate the Pine Tree State’s GOP chair previously dubbed "Maine’s Mamdani" to Fox News Digital, as debates over government intervention in housing and private ownership gain new attention.

"It’s a major issue. The greed that's happening right now in this country that people in mobile home parks are feeling is like something I've never seen," Jackson told a small crowd of residents at Blueberry Ridge Mobile Village, one of several Maine trailer parks where concerns about costs, quality-of-life and ownership arose.

MAINE DEMOCRATS CROWN TROY JACKSON AS PLATNER REPLACEMENT AS FRESH SCRUTINY CLOUDS SENATE RESET

"The other thing that I do hear a lot about, too, is how [landlords] won't do anything for services. And that is completely unfair and not right. And we have to make that change. I feel strongly that if needed, the state should be able to come in [and] take these places over. Some people will say that that's insane," Jackson told the residents in Wells, the town next to the politically-notable Kennebunkport.

"But until the people get the chance to start a co-op or whatever, there should be a way to hold these, so that you don't see private-equity coming in and making the killing on these parks."

PROPERTY OWNER ADVOCACY GROUPS PUSH BACK ON MAMDANI'S 'RENTAL RIPOFF REPORT,' PUBLIC DATABASE OF LANDLORDS

During his visit, Jackson held up a mason jar of brown water a resident said came from their tap.

Jackson said some residents saw their lot rental fees approach $850, adding he once lived at a mobile home park in Aroostook County and understands their plight.

"I’m going to add my voice to that every damn day," he said. "I just can't imagine owning a home and feeling the threat that you do daily and getting the squeeze and not being able to afford that."

Jackson’s proposal echoes one of the more aggressive elements of Mamdani’s housing agenda: a willingness to use government power to wrest control of troubled properties away from private owners and toward tenants, nonprofits or community stewardship.

MAMDANI RIPPED OVER 'FREAK SHOW' NEWS CONFERENCE WHERE EVICTION WAS DECLARED A FORM OF 'VIOLENCE'

Like Mamdani, Jackson was endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) in his prior unsuccessful gubernatorial primary bid earlier this year.

Mamdani’s Block by Block housing plan, released in May, calls for aggressive legal action against negligent landlords and says chronically neglected properties could be transferred to community land trusts, nonprofits or tenants.

BERNIE-BACKED SOCIALIST WHO ALLIED WITH PLATNER COULD SUPPLANT HIM ON BALLOT

"Through the Open-Door program and by supporting community land trusts, we will remove negligent owners and property managers of buildings suffering from chronic neglect or mired in foreclosure and shift ownership to responsible community stewards," Mamdani said in June.

While Mamdani’s more nationally-visible rent-freeze plans are materially different from Jackson’s considerations, they share a common thread: the government should intervene in the housing market when politicians believe pricing or practices are untoward.

MAMDANI’S $22 BILLION HOUSING LUNACY PROPOSAL WILL SOCIALIZE THE SKYLINE

That commonality led to Jackson being lambasted after the fact.

"Another full-on Communist running for office," said Lt. Col. Tony Shaffer [Ret.], a former intelligence officer, posted to X.

"Troy Jackson is ready to violate the rights of Mainers because he feels that they make too much money engaging in free market commerce," Shaffer tweeted. "Spoken here like the true Stalinist he is."

RESURFACED ASSAULT REPORT PUTS DEM SENATE NOMINEE IN GOP CROSSHAIRS: 'GRAHAM PLATNER 2.0'

The Republican National Committee also caught wind of Jackson’s comments, tweeting through their rapid-response arm.

"Troy Jackson wants the government to seize private property from Mainers," they wrote.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Maine law already gives mobile home park residents a limited pathway to take ownership when a park is put up for sale. Under Title 10, Section 9094-A, a group of mobile home owners or a residents’ association has the first option to purchase the park and generally has 60 days after notice of an intended sale to submit an offer.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jackson’s and Collins’ campaigns and Mamdani for comment.

item.title: Pamela Anderson reveals she drained her bank account to beat hepatitis C
item.description: Pamela Anderson linked her hepatitis C diagnosis to years of shame and guilt while delivering an emotional speech at the Venice Film Festival ceremony.
item.content:encoded:
Pamela Anderson paid a steep price to beat hepatitis C.

After living with the disease for years, the 59-year-old actress said she drained her bank account to pay for an early treatment that insurance didn’t yet cover.

Anderson opened up about her battle with hepatitis C and the shame she carried after her diagnosis in the late '90s while accepting amfAR’s Award of Courage on Sunday in Venice. The nonprofit, which works to end the HIV/AIDS epidemic, also supports hepatitis C research and advocacy.

RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD

"Back in the late '90s, when I was diagnosed with hepatitis C, there was no cure," Anderson said, according to multiple reports. "I'm sure that colored and corrupted my decisions. It was not fear of death but fear of what might happen to my young children. It turned my life inside out."

Anderson went public with her diagnosis in 2002 and claimed she contracted the disease while sharing needles with her ex-husband, Tommy Lee. The Mötley Crüe drummer has denied Anderson's claim.

When a cure eventually became available, Anderson said getting access required a major financial sacrifice.

"Ten blurry years later, there was a cure. I was lucky," she said. "I was offered it in its early stages, and it took everything I had in my bank to pay for it. It wasn't covered by insurance yet, and I felt tremendous guilt that others weren't granted the same access."

Anderson announced she was free from hepatitis C in 2015 after completing an FDA-approved yearlong regimen.

"But my experience of shame and guilt was also an unconscious journey. It stays with me; it haunts me," she continued.

"And just like the sexual abuse that I endured as a child, it felt like it was carved into my forehead: Damaged goods. And I presented myself as such."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Despite the challenges she faced following her diagnosis, Anderson eventually staged a major career comeback.

Since declaring herself "hep C free" in 2015, she has starred in "The Last Showgirl," "The Naked Gun" and "Rosebush Pruning." Her latest film, "Place to Be," premieres Wednesday at the Venice Film Festival.

"My truth has come through my work, finding ways to express myself through the arts. It gave me the ammunition I needed, a fertile life to use and play in," Anderson concluded.

"I’m not a victim, I’m a victor. I am strong and capable, more now than I could ever dream of … I’m not the damsel in distress, no matter how easy that role is to play."

item.title: Mom ‘very invested’ in Lindsay Clancy case hires Casey Anthony attorney after allegedly killing son: docs
item.description: Corie Walsh allegedly texted friends about the Lindsay Clancy murder trial just hours before her 2-year-old son Barrett was found dead in Frankfort.
item.content:encoded:
A Frankfort, Illinois, mother accused of killing her 2-year-old son had been discussing the high-profile Lindsay Clancy murder trial with friends just hours before the boy was found dead, court documents allege, and has hired one of Casey Anthony's former attorneys to defend her.

Corie A. Walsh, 38, later told officers she killed her son because she believed he was the "devil" and the "anti-Christ," a petition seeking to deny her pretrial release obtained by Fox 32 in Chicago states.

Walsh has been charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the death of her son, Barrett Walsh. The filing mentions her interest in the Clancy case but does not allege that it was connected to Barrett’s death.

ILLINOIS MOTHER CHARGED WITH MURDER IN DEATH OF 2-YEAR-OLD SON IN CASE DRAWING COMPARISONS TO LINDSAY CLANCY

Walsh’s attorney, Andrea Lyon, said she was "psychotic" and rejected any connection between her client’s interest in the Clancy case and the alleged killing.

"They are not correlated at all. It’s just accidental," Lyon said, calling speculation that Walsh’s actions were a copycat crime "baseless and cruel."

Court documents show Frankfort police officers were called to a home in the 22700 block of Brook Stone Court just after 4 p.m. Sept. 1 for a report of an injured child.

Upon arrival, officers found a neighbor performing CPR on Barrett after she reportedly discovered the toddler hanging from a basement rafter with his feet off the ground.

SUBURBAN ILLINOIS BOY DIES IN SUSPECTED DOMESTIC HOMICIDE AS NEIGHBORS FEAR ANOTHER LINDSAY CLANCY CASE

The neighbor brought Barrett down, laid him on the floor and attempted CPR while calling 911, later telling police the boy was cold and had no pulse. Barrett was pronounced dead at the scene, and a preliminary autopsy determined he died of asphyxia caused by strangulation, according to the filing.

Walsh’s three other children were unharmed, including an infant who was in the house at the time and two school-aged children who returned home around the time Barrett was found. Her husband was traveling out of state when the incident occurred and flew home that evening.

While officers were at the house, they were directed to an upstairs master bathroom where Walsh was reportedly trying to harm herself.

LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN

The petition states Walsh was lying fully dressed in a bathtub surrounded by bloody water while a neighbor held a towel against her left inner thigh. The neighbor told investigators she had disarmed Walsh of a knife and thrown it into a sink.

Police recovered the knife into evidence while documenting cuts on Walsh’s wrists and thighs, court documents state.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

The neighbor told investigators that Walsh asked why she had taken the knife from her because she was trying to kill herself. Walsh then said "Bear" was in the basement – referencing a known nickname for Barrett, the petition notes.

LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY

While hospitalized, Walsh made additional statements to investigators describing how she killed the toddler, which prosecutors noted were consistent with the physical evidence.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Witnesses told investigators Walsh had recently become "very invested" in the Clancy murder trial, which involved a Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three children.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Walsh allegedly discussed the Clancy case in a group text message with friends as recently as 12:30 p.m. Sept. 1 – roughly three and a half hours before Barrett was found. Her cellphone was recovered from the bathroom, and forensic analysis of the device was ongoing as of Sept. 3.

SEND US A TIP

Prosecutors are asking a judge to deny Walsh pretrial release, arguing that she poses a real and present threat to her husband and her three surviving children.

Walsh faces three counts of first-degree murder, with prosecutors outlining different legal theories regarding her intent. Because Barrett was 2 years old, a conviction carries a mandatory sentence of 60 to 100 years in prison without the possibility of early release.

Walsh remains hospitalized at Silver Cross Hospital and is expected to be transferred to the Will County Adult Detention Facility once medically released.

ACCUSED NC KILLER MOM PLANS INSANITY DEFENSE — AS RETIRED JUDGE SAYS MORE MAY FOLLOW LINDSAY CLANCY STRATEGY

Walsh’s defense team includes attorney Lyon, who previously represented Anthony. In 2011, Anthony was acquitted in the death of her 2-year-old daughter, Caylee, whose death remains unsolved. 

A jury found Anthony guilty of lying to law enforcement but not guilty of first-degree murder, aggravated manslaughter or aggravated child abuse.

The Will County State’s Attorney’s Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

At a detention hearing Tuesday, a judge denied Walsh’s request for pretrial release to a locked hospital setting. Lyon said the defense was disappointed but would continue investigating the case while Walsh recovers from her wounds.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Lyon said the defense will argue that Walsh was psychotic and that the charges do not amount to first-degree murder.

"She was psychotic. And this is not a first-degree murder," she told reporters.
