The defense may seek pretrial release again, Lyon said.

The case remains pending in Will County Circuit Court.

item.title: Jon Rahm dodges questions about wanting a pathway back to PGA Tour with LIV Golf future a complete unknown
item.description: Jon Rahm says he has "no updates" on LIV Golf's future ahead of the Irish Open, with bankruptcy concerns and funding questions looming large.
item.content:encoded:
With complete uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf and whether the circuit will even exist in 2027, the question of where LIV players tee it up next year remains top of mind. That's not just the reality from those on the outside looking in, because Jon Rahm doesn't appear to know where he'll be competing in the new year, either.

Rahm, who has won LIV's individual title every season since joining the circuit ahead of the 2024 campaign, is gearing up to play in a few DP World Tour events in the coming weeks. Speaking ahead of this week's Irish Open, he explained he has "no updates" about LIV and its future since the conclusion of the season in August in Indianapolis.

LIV Golf lost its funding from the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund (PIF) at the conclusion of the 2026 campaign. LIV CEO Scott O'Neil has announced that a new investor has been secured for "LIV 2.0" to take shape, but reports of a potential bankruptcy filing and funding question marks make the circuit's future uncertain, to put it mildly.

LIV GOLF CEO QUIETS SPECULATION WITH ANNOUNCEMENT OF NEW INVESTOR TO KEEP CIRCUIT AFLOAT INTO 2027

While Rahm's "no updates" remark was in response to the lone LIV Golf-related question he received during his formal pre-tournament press conference, BBC Sport pressed him multiple times about what his future may hold.

"There's just a lot of things in place. There's a lot of things that could happen," Rahm told the outlet. "It's one of those things with time, time's going to tell."

When asked if he would like to see a pathway back for him to return to the PGA Tour, the Spaniard didn't exactly offer a straightforward answer.

"I still have a contract with LIV 1.0 that I am more than willing to fulfill," Rahm began. "Like I said, time will tell."

When asked if he'd like to go back and play on the PGA Tour, he simply stated, "We'll see what happens."

LIV GOLF CEO SAYS LEAGUE IS HOPEFUL IT CAN 'DO RIGHT BY' VENDORS SUING THEM OVER ALLEGED MISSED PAYMENTS

Rahm is reportedly owed in excess of nine figures on his LIV Golf contract, and, to use his own phrase, time will tell if he will be compensated for his full deal if LIV files for bankruptcy.

On top of understandably practicing patience about being paid on his contract, there isn't much else Rahm or any other LIV player can do at this point when it comes to pledging allegiance to a certain side.

Just as it is entirely unclear what LIV 2.0 may or may not look like, it's also a complete unknown as to what a potential pathway back to the PGA Tour could look like for any players who jumped to the breakaway circuit. It is safe to assume some form of a pathway back will be offered to players, especially for a high-profile player such as Rahm, but until something takes shape, the wait-and-see game is the only one to play.

item.title: Drug developed for lung disease may slow biological aging in surprising ‘bonus’
item.description: Rentosertib, an AI-discovered drug for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, made patients appear three to four years biologically younger in a clinical trial.
item.content:encoded:
A drug being developed to treat a serious lung disease may also help to slow the aging process, researchers say.

In a small clinical study, patients who took rentosertib – developed by Insilico Medicine in Massachusetts – showed changes in blood proteins that made them appear biologically younger.

Several tests estimated that after treatment, the patients were biologically about three to four years younger.

EATING COMMON DAIRY FOOD EVERY DAY MAY SLOW BIOLOGICAL AGING, STUDY SUGGESTS

"There is a promising trend in age reversal in addition to treating the disease, and it came as a bonus for disease treatment," first author Alex Zhavoronkov, PhD, founder and co-CEO of Insilico Medicine, told Fox News Digital.

"It basically means that you are predicted to be younger using a validated set of aging clocks. We don’t know what that means yet."

The results were published in Nature Biotechnology and presented Monday at the Nature conference at Sorbonne University in Paris.

ALZHEIMER'S BLOOD TESTS MAY PREDICT SYMPTOMS YEARS IN ADVANCE, BUT EXPERTS URGE CAUTION

The researchers caution, however, that this does not yet prove the drug can actually reverse aging or help people live longer.

"It’s early days," Zhavoronkov noted. "The drug is still investigational."

Rentosertib is an experimental drug, discovered with the help of artificial intelligence, that is being developed to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a serious disease that causes scarring in the lungs.

In an unexpected outcome, the drug was found to change patterns of proteins in the blood in ways that made patients appear an average of three to four years younger, in one case up to six years.

Six different aging tests showed the same general pattern, with patients who took rentosertib "scoring" biologically younger than those who received a placebo.

The strongest effect was seen after four weeks in patients taking 30 mg of the drug twice a day.

LONGEVITY DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT MATTERS MOST FOR AGING WELL, BEYOND PRICEY BIOHACKS

When researchers compared the results with data from more than 55,000 people in the UK Biobank, they found that the drug changed several blood proteins in the opposite direction from what is normally seen with aging.

The researchers also found signs that the drug may affect aging at the cellular level, as it changed processes involved in how cells function and respond to damage.

Zhavoronkov said the company's approach uses AI to search for what he calls "molecular criminals" — biological targets that may contribute to both aging and disease.

The study – which was published in Nature Biotechnology – involved researchers from Insilico Medicine as well as Harvard Medical School, Stanford University, the Broad Institute, RWTH Aachen University, Peking University and Westlake University.

Zhavoronkov stressed that the findings are preliminary. "This is a pilot," he said. "It is early [and] exploratory."

The study had some limitations, including the small sample size – just 42 patients were analyzed over a 12-week period.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The participants all had IPF, which can change many of the same proteins researchers use to measure biological aging. This means it’s possible that the improvements in the participants’ lung disease was related to the changes in blood proteins.

The findings don’t prove that the drug actually slows aging, keeps people healthier longer or extends their lives, the researchers acknowledged.

The results were based only on changes in proteins in their blood, and do not yet support the use of rentosertib as an anti-aging treatment.

The risks and side effects associated with rentosertib were found to be "manageable," according to Dr. Carol Ann Satler, senior vice president of clinical development for Insilico Medicine.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The most common potential side effects included mild diarrhea, slightly lower potassium levels in the blood and temporary increases in liver enzymes.

"Once you stop the drug, essentially, they return to normal," Satler told Fox News Digital.

In the next trial, the doctor said, "We'll be looking to adjust the doses of the drug based on the side effect profile so that people can stay on it longer."

Rentosertib has now progressed into a year-long phase 3 study of more than 300 patients in China, according to Insilico.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Larger and longer trials – including healthy older adults and populations without IPF – are needed to determine whether the drug truly has anti-aging effects and whether they could lead to better health.

While more research lies ahead, Zhavoronkov said the findings have given him more confidence to continue pursuing drugs that could target both age-related diseases and aging itself.

"Everybody agrees that living longer should be a fundamental human right for everyone," he said.

item.title: Major blue state hospital pulls plug on controversial child transgender treatments after DOJ intervention
item.description: Mount Sinai, one of New York City's largest hospitals, agreed to stop sex reassignment procedures for minors and allocate $2 million for patient care.
item.content:encoded:
One of the largest hospitals in New York City will stop providing sex reassignment procedures to minors after entering an agreement with the Trump administration.

Mount Sinai has provided sex reassignment services, which included hormonal therapy and surgeries, to thousands of transgender patients. In 2025, Mount Sinai's Institute for Advanced Medicine reported that its providers saw 4,931 transgender and gender-diverse patients, but the exact number of minors receiving sex reassignment procedures has not been publicly disclosed, according to the hospital's report.

"The Department of Justice is committed to holding accountable medical providers that violate federal law and endanger children through so-called gender-affirming care," said Attorney General Todd Blanche. "This agreement puts an end to these practices at Mount Sinai and provides meaningful relief for individuals who have already suffered harm."

LARGEST CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL IN US TO OPEN ‘DETRANSITION CLINIC’ AFTER $10M SETTLEMENT WITH TRUMP DOJ, STATE

The agreement includes a monetary penalty and requires Mount Sinai to dedicate $2 million to free medical care for people suffering harmful consequences from transgender treatments they received as children. The agreement comes as part of an ongoing Justice Department investigation into hospitals providing such procedures to minors.

"A growing number of hospitals, like Mount Sinai, have recognized the medical scandal of sex-rejecting procedures," Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate of the Civil Division said in a statement. "While we are grateful when we secure resolutions to end this discredited practice and protect children, we must not and will not rest in our pursuit of justice for the victims it has left behind."

Curbing sex reassignment procedures for minors has been a top priority under the Trump administration.

JD VANCE CALLS ON DOJ TO PROSECUTE ALLEGED FRAUD IN TEEN TRANSGENDER TREATMENT

Just a week after being sworn into office, President Donald Trump issued an executive order titled "Protecting Children from Chemical and Surgical Mutilation," seeking to defund federal funding for gender reassignment procedures and directing the Justice Department to enforce the nation's female genital mutilation laws and investigate drug-safety violations and potential parental rights violations.

The Justice Department's investigation examines potential violations of the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the False Claims Act and other federal health care laws, including alleged fraudulent billing practices such as the use of false diagnosis codes to obtain payment from federal health care programs and private insurers, according to the department.

The executive order also directed federal agencies to rescind or amend policies that rely on guidance from the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH).

WPATH, a professional association that develops standards of care for transgender and gender-diverse patients, is being sued by the Federal Trade Commission and several states, which allege the group made false and unsubstantiated claims about the safety, effectiveness and medical necessity of pediatric medical-transition services. The case is pending.

COLORADO SUPREME COURT ORDERS CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL TO RESUME GENDER TRANSITION TREATMENTS FOR MINORS

WPATH's medical guidelines served as the bedrock for Mount Sinai's medical guidelines for transgender procedures, and Dr. Joshua Safer, executive director of the Mount Sinai Center for Transgender Medicine and Surgery, has co-authored WPATH guidelines.

The Justice Department did not release the details of the agreement with Mount Sinai but acknowledged that the hospital "remained cooperative, proactive, and solution-driven" at all times of the investigation.

"The settlement is complex, but at its core reflects Mount Sinai’s commitment to safeguarding our patients’ confidential information and protecting our clinicians," Mount Sinai said in a statement to the New York Times.

Mount Sinai's settlement is just the latest the Justice Department has reached with major hospitals providing transgender procedures. Texas Children's Hospital, the Cleveland Clinic Foundation and Connecticut Children's Hospital have agreed to halt youth transgender procedures in the past couple of months.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mount Sinai for comment.

item.title: Philippines defense chief calls out China after note interrupts remarks at Seoul forum: 'Coercion, bullying'
item.description: Gilberto Teodoro read aloud a note from China handed to him mid-speech at the Seoul Defense Dialogue, calling it actual coercion and bullying.
item.content:encoded:
Gilberto C. Teodoro, the Defense Secretary for the Philippines, publicly bashed China after he was handed a note outlining China's position on the South China Sea while he was speaking during the Seoul Defense Dialogue in South Korea on Tuesday.

While Teodoro was in the middle of speaking, a man in a white sports coat walked up behind him and placed a sheet of paper on the table beside him.

"I have a note here, I think this is from China," Teodoro said, stopping short in his remarks.

"And may I read it?" he asked the crowd, before proceeding to read aloud from the note.

"China's position on the South China Sea arbitration is clear, consistent and firm. They have no position. The arbitration violates fundamental principles of international law," the note read.

MASSIVE RISK IN SOUTH CHINA SEA EXPOSED AFTER FOUR-DAY POWER LOSS ON US NAVY DESTROYER

The note likely referred to the 2016 legal case that the Philippines brought against China under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). The case, titled the South China Sea Arbitration, determined that China was unlawfully reclaiming land in the Philippines' territorial waters.

China has long rebuked the ruling and consistently accuses the Philippines of infringing on China's sovereignty in the disputed waters.

The long-running dispute has created a number of tense standoffs between the two countries' navies.

"How can you deal with a country in an international forum – beyond the question asked to me – disrespecting the organizers of this forum, how do you expect to deal with it civilly?" Teodoro asked the crowd.

"I ask you the question, is this the right paper to post to me when I'm being asked a question on the floor? And how will you treat this kind of behavior? It not only disrespects, shows, if this is a Chinese position sent to me, it not only disrespects international law, throwing UNCLOS to the floor and trampling upon it, but it also disrespects the basic decency accorded that should be accorded to our most gracious host, the Republic of Korea and the rest of the audience here," he continued.

RULE JAPANICA: AMERICA AND JAPAN ARE BUILDING THE ALLIANCE CHINA FEARS

"So, perhaps basic decency and behavior is what China needs to do. This is actual coercion, bullying and aggression. I will keep this paper as a memento of how desperate China is and how ineffective its position is in the face of a free audience. Thank you very much for the person who gave me this piece of paper. You have just done your country a great service," Teodoro added.

"I think it is well known to the public, to everyone here about the Philippine situation where we face challenges daily from the People's Republic of China which tries to occupy and illegally assert its presence over our territory and especially our exclusive economic zone. In contravention with the UNCLOS. We live in a very interconnected world, and there is no right for any state of that matter to appropriate an international common for its exclusive use or right, contrary to what the international norms clearly state. So the Philippines has been forced to enter into creative defense arrangements and alliances," Teodoro concluded.

item.title: Reporter's Notebook: Dem rebels expose cracks in Jeffries’ House leadership
item.description: Jared Golden and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez blindsided Hakeem Jeffries by handing House Republicans a crucial procedural vote with zero warning.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Jared Golden, D-Maine, may retire from Congress next year with a reputation that is anything but gilded among his fellow Democrats.

Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, D-Wash., is seeking re-election in a competitive district. But some of her colleagues may consider "MGP" to be notorious if she returns to Capitol Hill in January.

The House of Representatives is now out — again — until Sept. 14. That follows a six-week sabbatical over the summer. But were it not for Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez, House Republican leaders may have had no other choice but to send members home early a few days ago. The duo committed something close to a parliamentary heresy, handing the GOP the necessary votes on a procedural matter to unlock the floor for the majority.

Republicans lacked the votes to do it on their own – had Golden and Gluesenkamp not intervened.

JEFFRIES THREATENS 'SERIOUS RESPONSE' AFTER DEMOCRATS HELP GOP ADVANCE ANTI-SOCIALISM VOTE

However, the most schismatic betrayal was that neither one briefed Democratic leaders on what they planned to do. Congressional leaders from both sides are never pleased with members who stray from the party line. Especially on a procedural vote, which is almost always the responsibility of the majority to pass. But at the very least, leaders like to be clued in. They might give someone a pass if they understand the reasoning.

"Did they give you a heads up that they were going to vote with Republicans on that rule?" asked Fox News' Kelly Phares of House Minority Whip Katherine Clark, D-Mass.

"They did not. They surprised us," answered Clark.

Yours truly observed to Rep. Tim Kennedy, D-N.Y., that in politics it’s always best to "stab someone in the front" rather than "in the back."

"There’s a lot to be said for that," replied Kennedy.

Let’s start with the nature of the dissent by Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez.

Most major pieces of legislation in the House need what's called a "rule" before the body can debate the measure. The House must debate and approve a "rule," dictating how much time and what amendments would be in order. The House can’t debate a bill until it first OKs a rule. And except on rare occasions, the majority party is expected to carry the rule. It’s simply something the minority party rarely assists with – except in extreme circumstances.

Last week, the House planned to debate a resolution to condemn socialism, green-light the SAVE America Act, maintain the number of justices on the Supreme Court at nine and consider a plan to help the nation’s lobster industry. The House adopted the rule, 210-208. However, five Republicans voted nay on the rule.

It’s about the math.

Those GOP defections would have killed the rule and frozen the floor for the rest of the week. In fact, the vote may have compelled House Republican leaders to cut everyone loose from Capitol Hill. The House was stalled considering any legislative traffic.

TENSIONS ERUPT IN HOUSE HEARING AS GOP ADVANCES ANTI-SOCIALISM RESOLUTION WHILE DEMS RAGE: 'SILLY SEASON'

But Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez voted yes, unlocking the floor for the remainder of the week.

Democrats seethed at their colleagues for blindsiding them.

"The two Democrats who have voted to move a procedural bill forward didn’t do the right thing," said Kennedy.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., Clark and House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., issued a rare, joint condemnation of the dissenting duo. They characterized the revolt "a significant breach of trust," adding it "necessitates a serious response."

"It’s a mistake to vote against our caucus. We have to be unified," said Rep. Madeleine Dean, D-Pa.

Golden said he voted with Republicans so the House could pass the bill safeguarding Maine’s lobster industry.

"It’s about protecting the working-class communities those men and women support. In my district, lobster fishing is the backbone of towns up and down the coast," said Golden. "In some towns, 20 to 40% of residents hold a lobster license."

Political observers view the infighting as a misstep for the party ahead of November.

"As a member, you should be able to communicate with your leaders and how you intend to vote," said Rep. Susie Lee, D-Nev. "Something was skipped along the way."

While some lawmakers blamed Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez, others said this was the fault of Jeffries. Others put it on Clark. Still, there were those pinning this on the entire leadership team.

Former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy, R-Calif., knows something about his own members undercutting him. Republicans stripped McCarthy of the speaker’s gavel nearly three years ago. But the California Republican believes the problem with Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez falls on the shoulder of Jeffries.

"You would know who would be the five to eight Democrats who would leverage that [vote]," said McCarthy. "You would have reached out to them."

One former Democratic aide noted that it wasn’t even what Jeffries, Clark and Aguilar said in their statement. But it was the very fact that a statement appeared. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., never would have sent a statement. Her leadership power was implicit. Everyone knew not to cross her. Or, if there was an issue, at least have a conversation.

HOUSE CONSERVATIVES DERAIL GOP AGENDA IN SAVE AMERICA ACT SHOWDOWN

Jeffries has not been the House’s top Democrat in the majority. That could change if Democrats win the House this fall. But McCarthy argued the statement said a lot about Jeffries.

"If Hakeem has to put out a statement that he's strong, it's a sign that he is weak," said McCarthy.

One senior House Democratic leadership source said rank-and-file members demanded accountability by Jeffries. Golden is done in January. Gluesenkamp Perez has repeatedly defied political gravity in a district which favors President Donald Trump. The source didn’t believe anything Machiavellian was afoot between Democratic leaders and Gluesenkamp Perez. But the source indicated that Gluesenkamp Perez tussling with the Democratic brass probably helps the Washington Democrat back home.

Still, some Democrats demanded retribution.

"I think there should be consequences. I think at the end of the day, we have a caucus united against what Republicans are trying to do," said Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee.

Actions speak louder than words. Remember that Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez voted against a "rule" in the House. Gluesenkamp Perez appeared at an unrelated meeting of the Rules Committee the next day. During her testimony, Rep. Jim McGovern, D-Mass., the top Democrat on the panel, swiveled around in his chair and sat with his back to his fellow Democrat.

Jeffries hoped to turn a corner with the renegades. He spoke briefly with Golden. But had a deeper conversation with Gluesenkamp Perez.

"Congresswoman Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and myself were able to talk in a very forward-looking way about how to make sure that we're all on the same page as we approach the midterm elections and beyond," said Jeffries.

He indicated that McGovern and Gluesenkamp Perez also talked.

But the leader was cryptic when pressed why he even had to issue an admonition.

HOUSE DEMOCRAT LASHES OUT WHEN GRILLED ON WHETHER SOCIALIST VICTORIES WOULD THREATEN DEM UNITY

"Does that say something about where the Democratic Caucus is and if they follow your leadership?" I pressed Jeffries.

"Res ipsa loquitur," answered Jeffries. "That's Latin for ‘the thing speaks for itself.’"

Not really.

Was the statement just a warning shot as Jeffries tries to flex his muscles in anticipation of becoming speaker and presiding over a Democratic majority next year? Where’s that "serious response" that Democratic leaders spoke of?

Some Democrats who are angry about the desertion will demand action. And if Jeffries doesn’t respond forcefully – despite a declaration otherwise – some members may interpret the warning statement as prattle.

That said, Democrats need Gluesenkamp Perez to win her district in order to claim the majority. And more specifically, Jeffries needs Gluesenkamp Perez to support him for speaker if Democrats have control next year and the margin is close.

Res ipsa loquitur? If Jeffries doesn’t take action – that speaks for itself, too.

item.title: Professional eater inhales a burrito to reclaim a title she had lost as world's fastest
item.description: Leah Shutkever reclaimed her burrito eating record at Guinness World Records HQ in London, dethroning Miki Sudo with a blistering 30.75-second time.
item.content:encoded:
Leah Shutkever has done it. The influencer/professional eater has set the world record for fastest time to eat a burrito for the third time to reclaim a title she had lost to speed eater Miki Sudo in 2022.

According to the Guinness World Records, she has 42 records to her name. Quite an accomplishment for someone who got into it by accident.

"My origin story of breaking Guinness World Records titles is one that I’ll never get bored of," Shutkever told Guinness World Records.

LAS VEGAS FOODIE EARNS GUINNESS WORLD RECORD AFTER EATING AT 28 TOP RESTAURANTS IN 24-HOUR SPRINT

"I had newly started up a YouTube channel doing food challenges, and I found an official record of fastest time to eat a Chocolate Orange, and I had a go, filmed it for YouTube, posted it, and thought nothing else of it."

She was then contacted by a TV show to make her attempt official, which she did. She's been hooked ever since she broke that record.

Shutkever first set the fastest time to eat a 1.35 pound burrito in 2019. She broke her own record with a time of 32.35 seconds in 2022, months before Sudo took it down.

In August, at the Guinness World Records HQ in London, she took back her title by inhaling a burrito in 30.75 seconds. An impressive feat that easily beat Sudo's time of 31.47.

What a performance by Shutkever. She left it all out there. Everything, but a single morsel of the burrito. That's how you take down one of 42 world records.

JOEY CHESTNUT REVEALS FOODS HE WON'T EAT IN COMPETITION AS HE TOURS MINOR LEAGUE STADIUMS FOR LOCAL DELICACIES

"I've been very fortunate in my career that many opportunities have landed on my desk, and I've been the right person with the right appetite to say yes to them," she said.

"Competitiveness definitely plays into the ability to attempt and break a world record. I think personally, I am silly, bold, and brazen enough to put myself in the firing line for all sorts of things."

That's how you humbly deliver a victory speech.

The ball is now in Miki Sudo's court or any other speed eater who thinks they have what it takes to barely chew a burrito and put it away in less than 30.75 seconds.

item.title: United flight attendant makes quick save, catching baby that was about to fall from 'exhausted' mom's lap
item.description: Monique Harris says she had no idea "being my normal natural self" would go viral after catching a baby on a United Airlines flight from Newark.
item.content:encoded:
A flight attendant aboard a United Airlines flight sprang into action when an exhausted mother dozed off and her baby began slipping from her lap — catching the child before offering to hold the baby so the weary mom could get some much-needed rest.

Passenger John Frehse shared the touching encounter on Instagram, praising flight attendant Monique Harris for her quick response aboard United flight 3486 from Newark, New Jersey, to Grand Rapids, Michigan.

"United should be very proud," Frehse wrote, adding that the new mother had fallen asleep when her baby was "about to fall out of her lap."

PILOT MARRIES VEGAS-BOUND COUPLE MID-FLIGHT AS 178 PASSENGERS BECOME WEDDING GUESTS

"Monique sprung into action and caught the child," he wrote. "She then told the mother to go back to sleep - she would give her a break."

Frehse also shared a photo appearing to show Harris holding the baby aboard the aircraft.

"All is not lost in the turbulent time," he wrote.

Frehse tagged United CEO Scott Kirby in the post and said he has flown more than 2 million miles with the airline.

"She is an A+ employee," he wrote. "Take note!!!"

RETIRED POLICE CHIEF HELPS SUBDUE PASSENGER AFTER ALLEGED MIDAIR OUTBURST OVER ALCOHOL CUTOFF

Harris responded to the praise in the comments, saying she was moved by the attention the moment had received.

"I’m in tears," she wrote, adding, "I never do anything for recognition."

Harris said she "had no idea that being my normal natural self would grow into such a priceless moment," and thanked Frehse and others for the comments.

Republic Airways, which operates flights for United and other airlines, praised Harris in an email to Fox News Digital.

"We agree with all the positive comments I saw on the post: Monique is an extraordinary colleague and flight attendant!" the carrier said.

The carrier also responded to the initial social media post, saying it was proud to have Harris on its team.

"Such a great story!" the airline wrote. "We are proud to have Monique on our team."

United Airlines responded to the post with a teary-eyed emoji.

item.title: Victims identified in fatal Amazon cargo jet crash at Miami airport
item.description: Five victims were identified after Amazon Air Flight 7598 overran the Miami International Airport runway, crashing into vehicles beyond the pavement.
item.content:encoded:
Authorities in Miami identified the five people killed when an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway while landing at Miami International Airport on Sunday, crashing into vehicles and catching on fire.

Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz released the names of the victims in a news conference on Tuesday.

They were identified as: Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Yoel Rodriguez Naranjo, 53; Julio C. Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and 47-year-old Javierkys Reyes Quevedo.

1 FOUND DECEASED AFTER 4 FAMILY MEMBERS FLYING FROM BAHAMAS TO FLORIDA IN SMALL PLANE GO MISSING

Five others were injured. Three of those people remain hospitalized, with two of them in critical condition. The two pilots were treated and released, the sheriff said.

Amazon Air Flight 7598 was traveling from San Juan, Puerto Rico, on its third flight of the day, when it tried landing at the Miami airport.

PILOTLESS CARGO AIRCRAFT COULD CHANGE HOW PACKAGES MOVE

The jet overshot the runway by at least 1,300 feet beyond the paved surface and crashed into multiple vehicles, including a 2012 white Ford Econoline van with passengers inside, National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said during a Monday press conference.

The aircraft then crashed through the airport perimeter and struck a civilian vehicle, a Toyota Corolla Cross LE.

UNITED AIRLINES JET FLEW TOO LOW AND TOO SLOW BEFORE STRIKING LIGHT POLE AND TRUCK NEAR NEWARK AIRPORT: NTSB

The plane then "continued into the grass and impacted another fence line, which separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed," Homendy said.

All the victims were inside the vehicles, she said.

Homicide detectives with the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office are investigating the deaths, Cordero-Stutz said.

Fox News Digital's Bonny Chu contributed to this report.

item.title: NATO member boots 10 Russian diplomats
item.description: Hungary demands that 10 members of the Russian mission leave the country, alleging that they engaged in actions that were "unacceptable," according to the Vienna Convention.
item.content:encoded:
Hungary has demanded that 10 individuals with the Russian mission depart the country.

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Anita Orban — who is not related to Hungary's former Prime Minister Viktor Orban — noted in a post on X that the 10 people had participated in actions that were "unacceptable" according to the Vienna Convention.

"Acting on my instructions, on Tuesday the relevant official from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs informed the Russian ambassador to Hungary that, according to the assessment of the Hungarian authorities, 10 members of the Russian mission had engaged in activities in Hungary that are unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention. The Hungarian side has therefore called on the individuals in question to leave Hungary," she declared in the post.

RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT

But Orban noted that Hungary is not cutting off diplomatic relations with Russia.

"This decision protects Hungary’s security and sovereignty. It does not imply breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia. Hungary intends to continue the necessary dialogue, based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules," she said in the post.

HUNGARY'S NEW LEADER ONCE IDOLIZED ORBÁN — NOW HE'S THE MAN WHO BROUGHT HIM DOWN

The Russian Foreign Ministry, in comments to Russia’s state news agency RIA Novosti, vowed to provide "an appropriate response" to the expulsions.

Hungary is a member of the European Union.

European Commission spokesperson Christian Wigand said Tuesday that "we take note of Hungary’s legitimate decision" to expel the Russian diplomats.

Wigand noted that the move was an expected response due to "Russia’s persistent campaign in using hybrid attacks against the EU and its member states."

RUSSIA'S QUIETER NUCLEAR SUBMARINES THREATEN NATO, FORMER COMMANDER WARNS

Hungary is a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), of which the U.S. is a founding member.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Erika Kirk pens essay on grief as readers gain insights into wrenching past year
item.description: Erika Kirk penned a New York Times essay on grief as the one-year anniversary of Charlie Kirk's fatal shooting at Utah Valley University approaches.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE — A year after Erika Kirk endured the unimaginable tragedy of her husband Charlie's assassination, she shared what she's learned about the universality of grief in a New York Times guest essay.

Kirk, who took over leadership of Turning Point USA (TPUSA) following the fatal shooting of her 31-year-old husband Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025, penned the piece Monday that's headlined, "What I’ve learned about grief."

She feels Americans increasingly experience each other through political labels and wanted to write something that reminds everyone that grief is something everyone can share.

ERIKA KIRK REFLECTS ON FIRST YEAR OF GRIEF AFTER CHARLIE KIRK'S ASSASSINATION IN NYT ESSAY

"You do not have to share someone’s politics, faith or worldview to understand what it means to lose someone you love. She wanted to meet people on common human ground and speak honestly about what the past year has been like," a TPUSA source told Fox News Digital.

Much of what she has been through over the past year is deeply familiar to anyone who has grieved, and she detailed how hard it was to make it through the first holidays and family milestones without her husband.

Erika Kirk explained why simply getting "through the next 15 minutes," which was advice from second lady Usha Vance, has been critical in getting through the past year.

JD VANCE'S WIFE USHA DETAILS HOW CHARLIE KIRK'S DEATH INFLUENCED DECISION TO HAVE FOURTH CHILD

"The first Saturday without a love note from him passed. His 32nd birthday. My birthday. Thanksgiving. When I put the Christmas tree together wrong, it made me realize that being a widow means old traditions will need to make room for new ones. The wave crashes on me again and again. Every time, just get through the next 15 minutes," Kirk wrote in the Times.

"Grief is strange. Time continues even when every part of you wants it to pause or, better yet, rewind. But the people we love who have passed on would not want us to spend the rest of our lives trying to rewind," she continued. "At first, I needed to survive the next 15 minutes. Over time, I’ve realized that Charlie would want me to live them."

Over the past 12 months, Kirk has tried to carry her late husband’s mission forward. She does not believe the answer to his death is to retreat further into separate camps where people only speak to those who already agree with them.

ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION

"He deliberately went into places where there was disagreement and invited people who saw the world differently to talk to him. He said, ‘When people stop talking, really bad stuff starts,’" the TPUSA source said.

Charlie Kirk founded TPUSA to promote conservatism on college campuses nationwide. He was speaking before more than 2,000 people at a TPUSA event in Orem, Utah, when he was assassinated, leaving behind Erika and their two children.

Fox News Digital’s Michael Sinkewicz contributed to this report.

item.title: Jelly Roll uninvited from law enforcement event after Trump jokes, but source says he had no knowledge of it
item.description: Jelly Roll was formally uninvited from a Mar-a-Lago law enforcement fundraiser after his jokes about President Donald Trump while guest-hosting "Jimmy Kimmel Live!"
item.content:encoded:
Country artist Jelly Roll was formally uninvited to a fundraiser at Mar-a-Lago in November hosted by Law Enforcement Today to support the Federal Law Enforcement Offices Association (FLEOA) Foundation on Friday, following his stint on Jimmy Kimmel's show.

Law Enforcement Today's Kyle Reyes told Fox News Digital that Jelly Roll didn't respond to the invitation sent on April 26, 2026, on behalf of FLEOA, but that they wanted to withdraw it in the wake of the Kimmel segment. The invitation, obtained by Fox News Digital, asked Jelly Roll if he would consider performing a few worship songs to close out the Big Blue Bash.

A source told Fox News Digital that Jelly Roll's team was never reached or spoken to about the November event and said they found out about it on social media.

The event is scheduled to take place in November at Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump's resort in Palm Beach, Florida. Law Enforcement Toady is running the gala to raise money for FLEOA and the FLEOA Foundation. The president of FLEOA said in a statement included on the Big Blue Bash invitation, "FLEOA is a non-partisan, professional association committed to supporting law enforcement across all agencies and administrations."

JOHN RICH CLAIMS JELLY ROLL KNEW HE’D LOSE HALF HIS FANS OVER POLITICAL COMMENTS

"It's a God-centered Gala and there's no better way to close out our event than with your voice," the letter to Jelly Roll read.

Reyes withdrew the invitation after the country music artist's stint on Kimmel's late-night show in August.

Reyes, who runs the Blue Lives Matter account on X, posted on Friday, "On April 26, 2026, we made the mistake of sending a formal invitation to country artist Jelly Roll to perform at this year's Second Annual Big Blue Bash at Mar-A-Lago, the home of President Trump."

"The event is a fundraiser for the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Foundation, a 501(c)(3) that takes care of the families of wounded and fallen officers," he continued. "Our organization, which owns the largest police news outlet in the world, is running the event. We'll be joined by the heads of all of the federal law enforcement agencies, sheriffs, police chiefs and supporters." 

"This year's theme is American Superheroes, and we'll be joined by superheroes such as Lou Ferrigno (The Incredible Hulk), Dean Cain (Superman) and Kevin Sorbo (Hercules). We're formally withdrawing the invitation for Jelly Roll," Reyes added.

The country star guest-hosted "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" and took aim at Trump's weight, physical fitness and approval ratings.

"Well, Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important. And trust me, you’ll be happy to see your penis again," Jelly Roll said. "It’s crazy. Think about this, y’all. In the last few years, I’ve lost 300 pounds. That means I’ve lost an entire Donald Trump."

JELLY ROLL PICKED A FIGHT WITH TRUMP FANS AND MAY HAVE BUD LIGHTED HIMSELF

"And let’s be honest, based on his approval ratings, it seems like most of the country wants to do the same thing," he added, before talking about the reaction to jokes he made about the president in a previous show, and said Trump should be able to "handle a few jokes."

During his final show filling in for Kimmel, Jelly Roll walked back his previous assertions that he is apolitical and said, "A lot of people seem to think these Jimmy Kimmel writers have secretly been pulling the strings and forcing this good old country boy to poke fun at our commander in chief."

"But let’s be real about this y’all: Do you think I would take orders from some sweaty little dork named Josh? No, I was just telling it like it is. And for some reason, that seemed to freak a lot of people out. I guess now that I’ve lost all this weight, folks can finally see I have balls," he said.

The country music star continued, "It is funny that before this week everybody thought I was MAGA. And now they think I’m some sort of liberal snowflake."

'NOT ON OUR WATCH': GLOBAL LAW ENFORCEMENT LEADERS UNITE IN POLAND AGAINST HATE

"Sure, I lean left on some things," he continued. "But like most folks, I’m pretty down the middle. I am a Christian. I am a country music singer. I’m a farmer. I’m a bow hunter. And most of the things I eat, I prefer to get with a stick and a string. That’s the truth."

He concluded the segment of his monologue by joking about his newfound friendships with Kimmel’s crew and said, "And I truly am going to miss all of my communist, Antifa friends here on the staff of ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’"

Reyes addressed the Trump jokes in his social media post, writing, "What I saw last week with this self-absorbed 'artist' bashing President Trump and Conservatives was not a man who walks in the footsteps of Jesus Christ — it was a man desperately seeking attention and relevancy from the very Godless crowd that has categorically rejected his preaching."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"We don’t hold Jelly Roll’s hate against him — but we sure aren’t going to welcome him into the home of the very man he decided to attack," Reyes told Fox News Digital. "And at the end of the day, his attack was a betrayal of his fans, his faith and all believers. We also aren’t going to allow a God-honoring event where we pay tribute to the families of fallen officers and pray over their families to be tarnished by a man who has lost his way."

Reyes said Rachel Holt and Coffey Anderson will be performing at the event, and there would be a surprise presentation from an American Idol star to honor the families of fallen officers.

FLEOA did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Craig Carton blasts Michigan fans for storming field after controversial win: 'They’re a bunch of morons'
item.description: Craig Carton ripped Michigan fans for storming the field after Bryce Underwood's controversial Hail Mary barely beat Western Michigan 13-12.
item.content:encoded:
Craig Carton scorched Michigan Wolverines fans for celebrating the team’s controversial victory against the Western Michigan Broncos on Saturday night.

There’s no argument that Michigan needed a little bit of luck to get past Western Michigan 13-12. Bryce Underwood received a second Hail Mary opportunity as officials determined that a Western Michigan defended touched his first throw in the final moments with one second left on the clock. Underwood found J.J. Buchanan for the game-winning score.

Is that a real reason to storm the field and act like you beat Ohio State? An emphatic no, says Carton, whose "Craig Carton Show" premieres on OutKick on Tuesday. Carton put it better than I could.

CRAIG CARTON: I'M BRINGING MY 'UNWAVERING, UNAPOLOGETIC' OPINIONS TO OUTKICK

"The thing that bothers me more than the hubris of adding a second to the game and giving Michigan another opportunity to win that game was the fact that there was 110,000 people at Michigan for that game and at the end of the game they stormed the field like they were Western Michigan knocking off a Big Ten team on the road," Carton said. "And it just was a good reminder to me that even though Michigan is thought of as a top educational experience for the kids that take the six years they normally take to graduate, the reality is that they’re a bunch of morons.

"Now, we already know that Michigan is a corrupt athletic program. We know that it’s a dirty athletic program. We know that coaches like to sleep with coeds there. Coaches like to steal signs there. Coaches like to cheat there. But what I didn’t know as a fact until Saturday night is that that 18-27 year olds that call Michigan their undergraduate home are morons. The fact that you would storm the field when barely beating and, let’s be honest, needing the Big Ten to cheat for you to win the game, the fact that you would storm the field when you won by a single point because you were given an extra second of time while 27-point favorites tells me everything I need to know about the type of kid that goes to Michigan."

SUBSCRIBE TO 'THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW' ON YOUTUBE

Remember, it’s not as though Michigan was unranked (they were 16th going into Saturday) and were up against Ohio State or Texas or Alabama or Oregon or even Rutgers for that matter.

The Wolverines were playing Western Michigan that plays in the Mid-American Conference and have been an FBS program since 1962. The Broncos have never beaten an opponent inside the top 20 of the Associated Press poll.

"That’s not a game to be celebrated if you’re a Michigan fan or a Michigan alumni," Carton added. "That’s a game to give you a warning about what’s to come for the rest of this season. Michigan football is dead. Michigan football is an embarrassment. Michigan football pays their quarterback $10 million a year and I would be better.

"So, just remember what you saw Saturday night. You saw a Wolverine program that needed cheating and needed secretive clocks to beat a MAC team while favored by 27 points. And the kids there are either so drunk, so high or so stupid that they stormed the field like they had accomplished something. You didn’t accomplish a damn thing but embarrassing yourselves on Saturday night."

Western Michigan has been ranked in the AP poll once ever – that coming in 2016 when they were 13-1 under P.J. Fleck. A victory over a blue blood would have been the biggest win in the program’s history.

The Big Ten and Mid-American Conference both released statements on the clock controversy after the game, reiterating that a Broncos defender touched the ball while out of bounds with one second left.

Michigan fans’ celebration was certainly silly and they will be needled for it until the next cray thing happens.

For now, the team itself has to prepare for noon ET showdown with Oklahoma on Saturday as questions surround Underwood about his status as QB1 for the future.

Michigan and Oklahoma will battle in Ann Arbor. The game can be seen on FOX.

item.title: Smithsonian head Lonnie Bunch to retire amid allegations of far-left woke messaging at museums
item.description: Lonnie Bunch III announced his retirement from the Smithsonian Institution amid an escalating clash with the Trump administration over museum leadership.
item.content:encoded:
The head of the Smithsonian Institution announced his retirement Tuesday, stepping down amid an escalating clash with the Trump administration over the leadership and direction of the nation’s museums.

Lonnie Bunch III, who has led the Smithsonian since 2019 and was the founding director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, said he will leave the post by the end of the year.

"It is with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude that I announce my retirement from the Smithsonian," Bunch said in a press release. "I have spent nearly half of my life working at and being part of the Smithsonian family, and what a privilege it has been. There is no place like the Smithsonian — it has been one of the great loves of my life, and I am extraordinarily proud of what we have accomplished together." 

SMITHSONIAN SHOWDOWN INTENSIFIES AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ISSUES A STARK NEW WARNING

"I leave with pride and sadness, gratitude and joy, and with enormous confidence in the people who will carry this remarkable institution forward," he added.

Bunch’s departure comes as the Trump administration has intensified scrutiny of the Smithsonian, accusing its leadership of allowing progressive ideology to shape its presentation of American history and raising concerns about potential violations of federal nondiscrimination law.

In a letter recently made public by the Department of the Interior, the administration said the Smithsonian leadership’s "institutional culture may have resulted in significant violations of Federal antidiscrimination law," including allegedly creating a hostile work environment and allocating opportunities, funding and other benefits based on race, ethnicity and other protected characteristics.

The letter did not include specific evidence of illegal activity, and the Department of the Interior did not provide further information when previously reached for comment by Fox News Digital.

The administration warned that federal agencies could withdraw certain forms of support if its concerns are not addressed, saying an "appropriate response" from the Smithsonian "must likewise address executive leadership and institutional ideology."

The pressure follows a 2025 executive order directing officials to seek the removal of what the administration called "improper ideology" from the Smithsonian.

SMITHSONIAN'S TAXPAYER FUNDS FACE CHOPPING BLOCK AS GOP DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY FOR 'WOKE' HISTORY

Bunch became the Smithsonian’s 14th secretary in June 2019, making him the first African American and first historian to hold the position. He previously led the creation of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, serving as its founding director from 2005 through its opening in 2016.

Bunch first joined the Smithsonian in 1978 and has spent nearly four decades at the institution, apart from a period when he served as president of the Chicago Historical Society.

Chief Justice John Roberts, who serves as chancellor of the Smithsonian, praised Bunch’s tenure and said the institution would work with him to ensure a smooth transition.

"From his days as a young curator at the National Air and Space and American History Museums through his tenure as the founding director of the African American History and Culture Museum and culminating in his distinguished service for the past seven years in the Smithsonian’s top job, Secretary Bunch has pursued excellence in the telling of our nation’s story," Roberts said.

Smithsonian Board of Regents Chair Franklin D. Raines said the board will announce an acting secretary and begin a national search for Bunch’s successor.

Fox News Digital’s Robert Schmad contributed to this report.

item.title: Families of 9/11 victims' message to Mamdani: 'Please do not come' to memorial ceremony
item.description: A 101,000-signature petition delivered to City Hall demands Mayor Zohran Mamdani skip the 25th anniversary 9/11 memorial service on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
A coalition of 9/11 family members, first responders, and elected officials gathered on the steps of City Hall on Tuesday to deliver a message to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani: stay away from this year's Sept. 11 memorial service.

"This mayor is not serving us," Charles Wolf, who lost his wife on 9/11, said at a noon news conference. "He's serving himself. We are asking respectfully that he not show up."

"Even though there is going to be other politicians there, these are the politicians that helped us push beneficial laws through and literally held our hand during that time," Wolf continued. "Mayor Mamdani has not shown any of that, none of it. He just wants to be there because he wants to be there."

"So we are asking him to respect the fact that that trauma is revived during the ceremony. It is a private ceremony. It is not a public ceremony. Mayor Mamdani, please do not come."

TRUMP POSTHUMOUSLY AWARDS MEDAL OF FREEDOM TO 9/11'S ‘MAN IN RED BANDANA’

New York City Council Member Vickie Paladino, a staunch, outspoken conservative, said she was leading organizers and family members into City Hall to formally deliver a petition with more than 101,000 signatures directly to the mayor’s office ahead of Friday’s 25th anniversary service.

"I am demanding that he not show his face at that sacred ground," Paladino said. "He does not belong there."

"We the people do not care for Zohran Mamdani – 101,000 names is not a drop in the bucket. Do not, Zohran Mamdani, take us New Yorkers for granted. We were there that day. The sky looked very similar to this. Stay put. Stay in City Hall and promote your propaganda."

Organized by Giovanni Galante — whose wife, Grace, was killed in the Sept. 11 attacks — the petition asks that the sacred anniversary remain a solemn, distraction-free day of mourning rather than a backdrop for political presence.

"We don't believe in what he believes in, and we really want us to be left alone," Galante said. "This 25th anniversary is for victims and survivors to blend in and pray that day for all the families — not have a circus around us."

MAMDANI UNDER FIRE AFTER SYMBOLIC 9/11 PEN GOES TO FORMER AL QAEDA DEFENSE LAWYER

The sentiment was echoed by other grieving family members who stressed that the Sept. 11 memorial service is a private, sacred space for victims' relatives to gather in peace.

"If we feel that we don't want someone at our world-class memorial museum that's sacred and hallowed, we feel that that person should respect our wishes," said Monica Iken, whose husband, Michael, was killed in the attacks. "He didn't go to the 20th … so I don't know why he's so adamant about going to this one when we just ask that he just respect us from 7 to 11 and let us have our mourning."

The objections stem directly from the mayor’s current policy positions, political associations, and key appointments, according to the speakers at the news conference.

Cheri Sparacio, whose husband, Tom, was killed in the South Tower, said the petition was not about the mayor's background or faith, but his public actions. She noted Mamdani’s appointment of chief counsel Ramzi Kassem — who previously represented individuals accused of terror ties — and his past ties to figures who have downplayed terror threats.

"That is what we object to," she said.

NYC Council Member Joann Ariola, also a Republican, accused the mayor of attempting to deflect from the families' concerns with performative announcements leading up to the event, rebuking the fact he has surrounded himself with advisers holding views hostile to core American values.

"Other politicians will be there, no one will speak — it is about the survivors and about those who were murdered that day," Ariola said. "Mayor Mamdani, for once, listen to your constituents and not your influencers and stay away from an event, a ceremonial commemoration of the lives that were lost on 9/11."

item.title: Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll aim to turn the Tennessee Titans into AFC South contenders
item.description: Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll lead a sweeping Tennessee Titans overhaul around Cam Ward, but the AFC South betting outlook hinges on key roster gaps.
item.content:encoded:
With defensive-minded head coach Robert Saleh taking over the program and veteran offensive coordinator Brian Daboll arriving to shepherd quarterback Cam Ward in his sophomore year, the Tennessee Titans are aiming to prove that its painful baseline rebuild is finally giving way to a competitive new era in the AFC South.

The Titans endured a brutal 2025 campaign, stumbling to a 3–14 finish and landing near the bottom of the league in both scoring offense and scoring defense. Rookie starter Cam Ward showed occasional dynamic flashes under pressure, while Tony Pollard provided steady work out of the backfield with a 1,082-yard rushing season. In fairness, the NFL didn’t do them many favors, giving them a really tough schedule even after a bad year. Ultimately, the lack of success on both sides of the ball led to the mid-season exit of Brian Callahan.

To reset the organization, general manager Mike Borgonzi orchestrated a sweeping offseason overhaul.

The headline moves started at the top by hiring former New York Jets head coach Robert Saleh as head coach and bringing in Brian Daboll to call plays. The problem I have is that neither has really proven successful with rebuilding teams – maybe Daboll more than Saleh.

JOSH ALLEN RECALLS HIS ROLE IN BILLS' COACHING SEARCH, DETAILS JOE BRADY’S APPROACH TO NEW ROLE

I do like teams that are intentional about upgrading areas. When you have a lot of areas to upgrade, there are only so many areas you can really make an impact. They signed former New York Giants wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson and tight end Daniel Bellinger, added edge rusher John Franklin-Myers and defensive tackle Solomon Thomas, and bolstered the secondary with cornerbacks Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott alongside safety Tony Adams.

They also brought in veteran quarterback Mitchell Trubisky as high-end insurance. In the draft, Tennessee made massive moves by taking wideout Carnell Tate at No. 4 overall and trading back into the first round for pass rusher Keldric Faulk. Major subtractions included letting lingering free agents walk and restructuring line depth to accommodate their fresh rookie class.

The offense features a far more dynamic receiving corps with rookie Carnell Tate on the perimeter alongside Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley, providing Ward with the quick-separation weapons he lacked as a rookie. Their line isn’t exactly top-notch, coming in at 29th for the year, but I do think there is potential they are better than they are graded at currently.

HOUSTON TEXANS' 2025 WIN TOTAL SET AT 9.5 AS CJ STROUD FACES QUESTIONS ABOUT OFFENSIVE LINE

If you plan to bet the over 6.5 wins for Tennessee, I think you attribute it to the improved weapons for Ward, the tough schedule from last season that still saw them get three wins, and the new coaching staff. If you want the under, it is looking at an offensive line that is ranked at 29th, and a defensive line ranked at 17th. The Texans have a great defense, but there are questions on that roster as well. The Colts have a quarterback coming back from an Achilles tear, and the Jaguars lost some key pieces. I have them right at six wins this year, which improves from last year, but I don’t think I can bet one way or another on them.

item.title: Alex Van Halen calls Sammy Hagar 'a complete idiot' as decades-long feud between bandmates deepens
item.description: Alex Van Halen called Sammy Hagar "a complete idiot" in a new interview, and Hagar fired back with a pointed Instagram comment over the weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Alex Van Halen has some thoughts about former bandmate Sammy Hagar.

During an interview with Brazilian music journalist Marcelo Vieira published earlier this month, Alex ripped into Hagar when asked about his 2011 memoir, "Red: My Uncensored Life in Rock."

"I don't know what he wrote, and I don't wanna know," he said, according to a translation from the original Portuguese interview published by Roadie Crew. "In my opinion, Sammy Hagar is a complete idiot."

SAMMY HAGAR BURIES DECADES-LONG FEUD WITH DAVID LEE ROTH AFTER TOUR DATES ARE AXED

Hagar has since responded to the insult, writing in an Instagram comment over the weekend, "This comment and post is so unnecessary at this time in our lives, but I guess the truth hurts sometimes. Peace already."

The latest jab comes after years of tension between the former bandmates, who have not spoken in more than two decades, according to Hagar.

ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK MAKES BLUNT ADMISSION ABOUT MYSTERIOUS DECADES-LONG TOM JONES FEUD

A representative for Alex did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Alex previously rejected an invitation to join Hagar and former Van Halen bassist Michael Anthony for their 2024 "Best of All Worlds" tour, which celebrated Hagar's era with the band.

"I'm not interested," Alex told Billboard at the time. "They're not doing the band justice. They can do what they want to do. That's not my business."

Alex also largely focused on Van Halen's original lineup with David Lee Roth in his 2024 memoir, "Brothers," while largely omitting Hagar's decade-long run with the band.

GEORGE MICHAEL STRUGGLED WITH 'ETERNAL CONFLICT' OVER FAME, WHAM! BANDMATE ANDREW RIDGELEY SAYS

"What happened after Dave left is not the same band," Alex told Billboard while promoting the book. "I'm not saying it was better or worse or any of that.… But the magic was in the first years, when we didn't know what we were doing, when we were willing to try anything."

Earlier this year, Hagar suggested he would "never play" with Alex again more than 20 years after their last tour together.

"I'm the biggest Pink Floyd fan. I see David Gilmour say, 'I will never play with Roger Waters again,' and I know what he means," the 78-year-old told Classic Rock. "I feel that way about Alex Van Halen. They're negative people."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Hagar, who replaced Roth as lead singer of Van Halen in 1985, remained with the band until 1996. He later reunited with the group in 2004 for a reunion tour.

The singer has suggested that Alex's health problems and inability or unwillingness to continue playing drums may have contributed to the tension. Hagar speculated that Alex could be frustrated that he and Anthony continue to perform Van Halen songs while the drummer is no longer touring.

Hagar told Rolling Stone in April 2025 that he and Alex had not spoken in 21 years.

"I hate to say it, but I dreamt about Alex the other night, man," he told the magazine. "It was crazy. And it was so friggin' real. I was saying, 'What are you p---ed off at me about, man? What the f---? Now, just tell me what your problem is. What did I do? Just tell me.'"

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Hagar said he thinks Alex is upset with him "because I'm out doing it, and Mike [Anthony] and I are out doing it, and he can't. He's not a singer. He's not a guitar player. He is not really a band leader. And he seems like he doesn't want to play drums or can't play drums anymore, and he can't go write a new record."

"Alex wasn't the songwriter in the band," he continued. "He was the drummer. Eddie and I wrote the songs. Dave [Lee Roth] and Eddie wrote the songs, and so we can go out and do them. And I think that really bothers him that Mike and I are still out there doing it. I would feel bad. If I put myself in his shoes, I would feel terrible if I couldn't do it anymore."

Alex's criticism also follows Hagar's previous claims that he tried repeatedly to reconnect with his former bandmate, including while assembling the "Best of All Worlds" tour. Hagar said he and Anthony reached out to Alex "a dozen times" before the tour but received no response.

item.title: Viral Ole Miss fan goes through her favorite DMs since being discovered during win over Louisville
item.description: Sara Smith, the viral Ole Miss fan from the Liberty Mutual Music City Kickoff, shared her wildest DMs on TikTok after the internet identified her.
item.content:encoded:
What a week of action to officially start the college football season. We had a mysterious second appear and the sad storming of the field that followed in Week 1 of the season.

There was the pure theater in Baton Rouge, a power outage on Monday night in Tallahassee, and a great back-and-forth game between Louisville and Ole Miss that produced the first viral fan of the season on Sunday night.

Cameras spotted the Ole Miss fan during the third quarter of the Liberty Mutual Music City Kickoff in Nashville as she was showing concern for the Rebels' inability to put the Cardinals away.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The internet worked its magic and identified her a short time later as Sara Smith. The Ole Miss alum went private on Instagram, but evidently not before she received several DMs.

On Monday night, on TikTok, Smith acknowledged that she was the hot viral Ole Miss fan who became an internet star thanks to a few seconds of camera time and the power of social media.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

She also wanted to go through several of her favorite DMs that showed up over the last 24 hours. A God-fearing business owner slid in with his "credentials," including that he was over six feet tall and took home $500k annually.

An offer to pick her up something from Whole Foods made her list of favorites, as did an intriguing offer that simply read "Bankrupt me."

From there, Smith had your standard "Let's make (baby emoji)'s" and the "what type of bag can I buy you from Paris" type questions show up. You know, more run-of-the-mill sorts of DMs. Traditional, if you will.

There were a couple of bizarre ones that made the list, as you might expect. Like one mentioning clouds and another that offered to save her. It wouldn't be social media without at least one DM calling her armpits overrated.

One of those made her list, as did one calling for her to become a model for brands like Gucci. Why not? We've seen crazier things happen thanks to a viral moment on social media. Best of luck to Sara Smith and Ole Miss this season.
